programs.name: HFSP Research Grants & Postdoctoral Fellowships
programs.desc: Funds international, interdisciplinary teams of 2–4 PIs doing basic 'frontier' life science — no applied, clinical, or drug-development work — plus postdoctoral fellowships requiring an international move.
programs.eligibility: Research Grants: independent lab heads anywhere, with at least one member in an HFSP member country; teams should be intercontinental with no substantial prior joint publications. Early Career variant: all members ≤5 yrs independent and ≤10 yrs post-PhD. Fellowships: PhDs changing fields and countries.
programs.apply: Two-stage via ProposalCentral: LOIs initiate ~mid-March annually (grants) and ~May (fellowships); invited full proposals in September; awards the following March.

dates.label: Research grant letter of intent expected
Postdoctoral fellowship letter of intent expected

programs.bths: A mechanistic cardiolipin-biophysics collaboration, such as a US biologist with an EU physicist, qualifies. A translational BTHS therapy project does not.

programs.name: Experiment.com Science Crowdfunding
programs.desc: All-or-nothing crowdfunding for small research projects, with roughly a 48% success rate; junior investigators outperform senior ones. Typical uses are pilot data and trainee side-projects, and amounts are small relative to grant funding.
programs.eligibility: Any researcher; projects are reviewed for scientific clarity and feasibility before going live. No institutional restriction.
programs.apply: Projects are created at experiment.com — free to start; 8% platform fee plus ~3–5% payment processing on successfully funded projects only.
programs.bths: Rare-disease campaigns benefit from an engaged patient community, and BSF's network can amplify a campaign — which is the main reason this works better for BTHS than the raw success rate suggests.

programs.name: RARE Impact Grants (for advocacy organizations)
programs.desc: Grants to patient advocacy organizations in Global Genes' Global Advocacy Alliance, for education, patient support, and research-advocacy capacity.
programs.eligibility: Rare-disease patient advocacy organizations that are members of the Global Advocacy Alliance.
programs.apply: Via the Global Genes prospectus/application when cycles open.
programs.bths: Relevant to the Barth Syndrome Foundation as an organization rather than to individual labs. Not investigator-initiated science.

programs.name: EveryLife Foundation Programs (advocacy & policy)
programs.desc: Policy and regulatory advocacy support rather than bench research. The Rare Giving program funds advocacy groups and patient advocates, covering travel, survey tools, and IRB and publication fees for patient-experience data. #RAREis Scholarships support students living with rare diseases.
programs.eligibility: Advocacy organizations and patients, not scientists.
programs.apply: Through the program pages at everylifefoundation.org.
programs.bths: Applies to BSF policy work such as newborn screening, and to community members as scholarship applicants. Not a route to lab funding.

programs.name: BSF Emergency Relief Program
programs.sponsor: Barth Syndrome Foundation, administered by NORD
programs.amount: Short-term emergency assistance (fund sized for ~20 families/yr)
programs.desc: Short-term cash assistance for unexpected, non-medical emergency expenses. Established 2022. BSF funds the program and NORD administers it, so families can apply privately, with eligibility screened by NORD patient services.
programs.eligibility: Families affected by Barth syndrome who meet NORD's eligibility screening.
programs.apply: Call NORD Patient Services at 1-203-292-0293 (Mon–Thu 8:30–7 ET, Fri 8:30–6 ET) or email barthsyndrome_assist@rarediseases.org.
programs.bths: Barth-specific by design and restricted to affected families — the most direct financial help BSF offers, and private by construction.

programs.name: BSF Family Services & Conference Support
programs.amount: Support services; subsidized conference registration + limited scholarships
programs.desc: Family services include information and guidance, one-on-one emotional support, private family communities, and the membership registry. The biennial International Scientific, Medical & Family Conference offers heavily subsidised family registration ($50–150 per person in 2026), free Camp Barth childcare during sessions, and a limited number of family scholarships each cycle.
programs.eligibility: Families affected by Barth syndrome. Barth Syndrome UK offers free membership, private groups, and weekly online meet-ups for UK families.
programs.apply: Contact BSF through barthsyndrome.org; watch barthsyndromeconference.org and the BSF newsletter for the next conference cycle.
programs.bths: Barth-specific by design. The 2026 conference ran July 19–26; the next is in 2028, with scholarship details published per cycle.

programs.name: NORD RareCare Patient Assistance Programs
programs.amount: Varies by fund; first-come while funds last
programs.desc: NORD's assistance portfolio covers medication costs, insurance premium and copay assistance, diagnostic testing, travel for clinical trials or specialist consultations, and limited travel and lodging for rare-disease educational conferences.
programs.eligibility: US residents of all states and territories; per-fund financial screening applies.
programs.apply: Call 1-800-999-6673; a RareCare Patient Services Representative walks applicants through the process.
programs.bths: Open to Barth families as a rare disease. Note that Barth families also have the dedicated BSF-funded emergency fund, listed separately, which is often the faster route.

programs.name: Patient Advocate Foundation — TotalAssist & Case Management
programs.sponsor: Patient Advocate Foundation (merged with PAN Foundation 2026)
programs.amount: ~150 disease funds; grants for copays, premiums, visit costs
programs.desc: Following the PAF–PAN merger, new financial applications route through TotalAssist as of July 1, 2026: roughly 150 disease-specific and health-equity funds covering medication copays, coinsurance, deductibles, insurance premiums, office visits, and treatment administration. Separately, PAF case management is free to any US patient with a chronic or debilitating illness, and is the main free help available for insurance denials, prior-authorization fights, appeals, and billing negotiation.
programs.eligibility: US patients; per-fund financial and diagnosis criteria. Case management has no fund requirement.
programs.apply: Apply online at patientadvocate.org or by phone via the site.
programs.bths: Whether an open fund currently matches Barth syndrome changes weekly, so check the fund finder. Case management does not depend on a matching fund and is available regardless.

programs.name: HealthWell Cardiomyopathy — Medicare Access Fund
programs.deadline: CLOSED to new patients (insufficient funding) — reopens only when refunded
programs.desc: A copay fund covering prescription copays or Medicare Part B premiums for cardiomyopathy patients on Medicare, up to $7,500, for household income up to 500% of the federal poverty level. More than 100 cardiomyopathy medications are covered, including beta blockers, ACE inhibitors, diuretics, anticoagulants, Entresto, Vyndaqel, and Corlanor. As of Aug 28, 2026 the fund is temporarily closed to new patients for lack of funding; existing grantees keep their benefits through their 12-month cycle. HealthWell funds reopen without notice when refunded, so it is worth re-checking rather than writing off.
programs.eligibility: Medicare beneficiaries with cardiomyopathy; income at or below 500% of the federal poverty level, adjusted for household size and cost of living; treatment in the US.
programs.apply: Apply online or call (800) 675-8416.
programs.bths: Relevant to adult Barth syndrome patients on Medicare, for example through SSDI, since cardiomyopathy is the qualifying condition. HealthWell has no mitochondrial-disease-specific fund, and its General Travel Fund (up to $500) requires a prior HealthWell grant and was also reported closed to new patients.

programs.name: Marcel's Way Family Fund & Mito411
programs.desc: One-time need-based grants up to $500 for mitochondrial-disease-related costs: uncovered medical expenses, lodging during treatment, equipment, home or vehicle modifications, and respite. One grant per patient lifetime, requiring a physician letter and a community-professional letter. Applications are currently closed. MitoAction's Mito411 helpline (1-888-648-6411) and weekly support groups remain active.
programs.eligibility: US residents with a diagnosed mitochondrial disorder, which includes Barth syndrome.
programs.apply: Check the fund page for reopening; the Mito411 helpline operates regardless.
programs.bths: Barth syndrome qualifies as a mitochondrial disease when the fund reopens; the helpline and support groups are available now regardless.

programs.name: Mito Assist — FORZINITY Patient Support
programs.amount: Copay assistance; free drug for uninsured/underinsured
programs.desc: The patient support program for FORZINITY (elamipretide): insurance benefits investigation and submission support, copay assistance for commercially insured patients, a patient assistance program providing free drug to uninsured or underinsured patients, at-home subcutaneous injection training, and dedicated case management. AnovoRx is the exclusive US specialty pharmacy. Copay caps and income criteria are confirmed at enrollment and are not published.
programs.eligibility: US patients prescribed FORZINITY (approved for patients weighing at least 30 kg); program tier depends on insurance status.
programs.apply: Call 1-833-458-9099 or start with the Patient Enrollment Form on the AnovoRx site, typically initiated with the prescriber.
programs.bths: FORZINITY is the approved Barth syndrome treatment, so this program exists specifically for BTHS patients starting or continuing on it.

programs.name: G-CSF Assistance — Amgen SupportPlus & Safety Net Foundation
programs.amount: Copays to as little as $0; free drug via Safety Net
programs.desc: Two routes to affording G-CSF (NEUPOGEN/Neulasta). The SupportPlus Co-Pay Program lets commercially insured patients pay as little as $0 per dose, applied to deductible, coinsurance, or copay; it is not valid for Medicare, Medicaid, or cash payers. The Amgen Safety Net Foundation provides free Amgen medicines for uninsured or under-covered patients.
programs.eligibility: SupportPlus: commercial/private insurance only. Safety Net: US residence for 6+ months, household income at or below 400% of the federal poverty level, generally not eligible for public coverage (certain Medicare patients with coverage gaps may qualify).
programs.apply: SupportPlus: enroll online or call (866) 264-2778. Safety Net: 1-888-4ASSIST.
programs.bths: G-CSF is the standard treatment for Barth syndrome neutropenia, which is what brings these programs into scope. Families prescribed a filgrastim biosimilar such as Zarxio or Nivestym should ask the prescriber which manufacturer's program applies instead.

programs.name: #RAREis Scholarship
programs.desc: One-time $5,000 scholarships for students living with any rare disease. The program has awarded nearly 500 scholarships since 2020 and is administered by Scholarship America. The 2026 application window ran March 17 to April 28.
programs.eligibility: US residents age 17+, physician-diagnosed with a rare disease, enrolling full- or part-time at an accredited 2- or 4-year college, university, or vocational-technical school.
programs.apply: Apply via Scholarship America when the window opens (typically March).

dates.label: Next cycle expected to open
dates.note: The 2026 cycle closed Apr 28, 2026.

programs.bths: Barth syndrome qualifies as a rare disease; the scholarship is disease-agnostic.

programs.name: Mitochondrial Disease & Neuromuscular Student Scholarships
programs.amount: MDA up to $5,000; Harty amount varies
programs.desc: Two student scholarships. The Matthew Harty Scholarship (MitoAction) is for high-school seniors or enrolled college students diagnosed with mitochondrial disease, with over $200,000 awarded since 2015; the 2026 cycle closed May 31. The MDA College Scholarship is merit-based, up to $5,000, for students with an MDA-supported neuromuscular disease; the 2026 deadline was March 15.
programs.eligibility: Harty: students diagnosed with mitochondrial disease. MDA: US citizens or permanent residents with an MDA-covered disease; no age limit.
programs.apply: Both recur annually; apply on each organization's scholarship page when windows open.
programs.bths: A Barth syndrome student qualifies for the MitoAction scholarship as a mitochondrial disease. For the MDA award, confirm whether MDA classifies Barth syndrome as covered at ResourceCenter@mdausa.org before applying.

programs.name: Medical Travel & Lodging Assistance
programs.sponsor: Miracle Flights, Angel Flight network, Mercy Medical Angels, RMHC
programs.amount: Free flights, ground travel vouchers, lodging
programs.desc: Four routes to distant specialist care. Miracle Flights provides free commercial airline tickets for children 17 and under plus parents, requiring a confirmed appointment, medical clearance, income at or below 370% of federal poverty guidelines, and 14+ days' notice. Angel Flight regional charities fly patients free in small aircraft with volunteer pilots, requiring a physician release and at least 5 business days' notice — these are regional, so use the one covering your state. Mercy Medical Angels provides gas cards, Uber and Lyft vouchers, bus and train tickets, and flights for appointments 50+ miles away. Ronald McDonald House provides lodging near children's hospitals, free or for a small suggested donation, requested through the treating hospital's social work team.
programs.eligibility: Varies by program: age limits (Miracle Flights: 17 and under), income verification (Miracle Flights, Mercy Medical Angels, some Angel Flights), distance rules (Mercy: 50+ miles; some RMHC Houses).
programs.apply: Each program takes online requests; Ronald McDonald House goes through hospital social work.
programs.bths: Barth syndrome care is concentrated in a small number of specialist centres, so travel is a recurring cost for most families rather than an occasional one.

programs.name: Make-A-Wish & Starlight Children's Foundation
programs.desc: Make-A-Wish grants wishes for children roughly 2.5–17 at referral with a critical illness — progressive, degenerative, or malignant life-threatening conditions. The child need not be terminal, and there is no cost or income test. Starlight delivers in-hospital programs including gaming stations, VR, hospital gowns, and toy deliveries at 800+ US facilities, and families can join the free Starlight Families program for at-home resources.
programs.eligibility: Make-A-Wish: children ~2.5–17 with a qualifying condition, one wish per child. Starlight: via participating hospitals, plus the free family program.
programs.apply: Make-A-Wish referrals come from a parent or guardian, medical professional, or the child at wish.org/refer-a-child.
programs.bths: Barth syndrome with cardiomyopathy has historically qualified for Make-A-Wish; the determination is made by the child's treating physician with Make-A-Wish medical review.

programs.name: SSI & Medicaid Waivers (Katie Beckett / TEFRA)
programs.sponsor: Social Security Administration / state Medicaid agencies
programs.desc: Two government benefits. SSI childhood disability provides income support subject to family income and asset limits. Katie Beckett/TEFRA Medicaid lets a child with institutional-level care needs get Medicaid counting only the child's own income, regardless of parental income — valuable for families over SSI limits, covering copays, nursing, and equipment as secondary insurance. About 18 states plus DC have the classic TEFRA option; others run similar waivers, some waitlisted.
programs.eligibility: SSI: children meeting SSA's disability standard, subject to family income/asset limits. Katie Beckett/TEFRA: children needing an institutional level of care; rules vary by state.
programs.apply: SSI: ssa.gov/apply or 1-800-772-1213. Katie Beckett/TEFRA: through the state Medicaid agency; kidswaivers.org has a state-by-state directory.
programs.bths: Barth syndrome is not on SSA's Compassionate Allowances fast-track list, verified against the April 2026 list, so SSI applications go through standard childhood disability evaluation — typically documented through the cardiomyopathy and heart failure, growth failure, and recurrent-infection listings.
